locator.text: Equation (7.20), p. 79, in the proof of Proposition 7.2

evidence: paper: (D^I z_m)' = A_m D^I z_m + D^I g_m + \sum_{0<J\le I} \binom{I}{J} (D^J A_m) D^{I-J} z_m.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same equation, written with ordered words of directional derivatives instead of multi-indices. jet_solution_hasDerivWithinAt says (D^I z)' = A·D^I z + jetSource, and jetSource = D^I g + crossJet; productJet_split is the Leibniz identity D^I(Az) = A·D^I z + crossJet. The paper's binomial multiplicity (I choose J) is produced by counting ordered words rather than written as a coefficient: productJet enumerates all 2^{|I|} ordered choices of which factor each derivative hits (its docstring: 'retaining ordered differentiation and therefore automatically retaining every mixed-term multiplicity'), and crossJet is the subsum with at least one derivative on A, which is Σ_{0<J≤I} (I choose J)(D^J A)D^{I−J}z. The paper's side condition that D^I differentiates only parameters, holding v fixed, and commutes with ∂_v, is structural in Lean: the parameter space P and the time variable t ∈ Icc a b are separate arguments. The Lean derives the equation for the constructed solution family rather than assuming the jets exist (jet_solution_eq_solution), which is if anything more than the paper asserts here.
